newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt finalises law on exiled king's return.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt finalises law on exiled king's return.

text.p: The Italian cabinet on Friday finalised a draft law which would allow the son of the last king to come home, half a century after the monarchy was abolished and all male heirs barred entry.

The centre-left cabinet drew up a bill which, if passed by parliament, would allow Vittorio Emanuele, 59, to return to Italy after he was forced into exile with his father, King Umberto II, as a nine year-old.
Members of the House of Savoy would not, however, be allowed to take part in political activity, or to vote in the Italian republic which replaced the monarchy in 1946 after a referendum.
War-weary Italians blamed their royals for complicity with more than 20 years of fascist rule under dictator Benito Mussolini, who led Italy into World War Two on the Nazi side.
The cabinet said in a statement that the draft bill, which must be passed by both houses of parliament before it can become law, was not an attempt to rewrite history.
"The law does not represent...any revision of ethical and political judgements on events which are consigned to history," the statement said.

Vittorio Emanuele, who is living in Switzerland with his family, caused outrage last week when he refused to apologise for anti-semitic laws passed in 1938 under fascist rule when his grandfather, Vittorio Emanuele III, was head of state.
The leader of Rome's Jews, Rabbi Elio Toaff, called the laws, which threw Jews out of schools and jobs, a "disgrace which cannot be erased from the history of the House of Savoy".

The hard-left Communist Refoundation party, whose support gives Prime Minister Roman Prodi a parliamentary majority, said earlier this week it was opposed to the return of Vittorio Emanuele in the light of his comments.
"It is an unheard-of disgrace that he did not say sorry to Italians for the racial laws and for taking Italy into war," Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said.
